subject: Svenska
title: Reading comprehension
sourceSummary: Main message, conclusions and summarising — reading between the lines and distinguishing what a text says from what it implies.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Many teenagers exercise less today than ten years ago. School sports have declined, and fewer join sports clubs. At the same time, surveys show that mental ill health among young people is rising. Researchers believe the connection is no coincidence."

What is the main message of the text?
questions.opener: The last sentence usually ties together the point of the text — what does it say?
choices: School sports should be compulsory
There is probably a connection between reduced physical activity and mental ill health among young people
Sports clubs are the best way to exercise
Mental ill health has always existed among young people
questions.explanation: The text builds up a connection between reduced exercise and increased mental ill health, and ends by saying researchers believe there is a link. That is the point of the text — not a demand for compulsory sport, which is never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Emma looked at the clock for the third time. She had already packed her bag twice and put the same jumper back. When her mum called that the car was ready, she rushed down the stairs without tying her shoes."

What can be concluded about Emma?
questions.opener: What does it reveal that she repacks the same bag and forgets to tie her shoes?
choices: She is tired and wants to sleep
She is angry at her mum
She is nervous or excited about something
She has forgotten where they're going
questions.explanation: Checking the clock repeatedly, repacking, and rushing without tying her shoes signals nervousness or anticipation — the text never states this directly, but the details all point the same way.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Picking berries in the forest requires no membership, fee, or special equipment. The right of public access gives everyone in Sweden the right to be in nature and pick berries and mushrooms, as long as they don't disturb or damage anything."

Which summary fits best?
questions.opener: Which sentence in the text explains WHY you can pick berries freely?
choices: Picking berries is free if you have the right equipment
The right of public access makes it possible for everyone to freely be in and pick from nature, within certain limits
You must be a member of a club to pick berries
Mushrooms and berries may only be picked by the landowner
questions.explanation: The text explains that the right of public access provides free access — but with the condition "as long as they don't disturb or damage anything", which option 1 leaves out.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The school library has extended its opening hours following requests from students. Books can now be borrowed even in the morning before lessons start, not only during free periods as before."

Which headline best summarises the text?
questions.opener: A good headline captures WHAT has changed and WHY.
choices: The school library is being rebuilt
More books for the school library
The school library has longer opening hours following student requests
Students can no longer borrow books during free periods
questions.explanation: The text is specifically about extended opening hours because of student requests — not a rebuild, more books, or free periods being removed (the morning slot is an ADDITION, not a replacement).

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The restaurant already had a queue at eleven in the morning, even though it had only opened a week earlier. The owner smiled broadly as she counted the guests."

What does the text suggest about the restaurant?
questions.opener: What do the queue and the owner's smile say about how the restaurant is doing?
choices: The restaurant doesn't have enough staff
The restaurant already seems to be popular and doing well
The restaurant will close soon
The owner is unhappy about the queues
questions.explanation: The queue despite the restaurant being new, plus the owner's smile, suggests success — the text never states this directly, but the details clearly point that way.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Many people believe you think best in silence. But studies show that some people actually solve problems faster with background noise, like the faint hum of a café. Silence doesn't suit everyone equally well."

What is the point of the text?
questions.opener: The text starts with a common belief and then turns it around — what is the conclusion?
choices: Everyone thinks best in a café
Silence is always best for concentration
What helps concentration varies from person to person
Background noise always disturbs concentration
questions.explanation: The text challenges the assumption that silence is always best and shows that it varies between individuals — that is the point, not that cafés are generally better.

questions.prompt: Summarise the text in no more than two sentences: "The municipality has decided to build a new cycle path between the school and the town centre. The decision came after several parents complained that the children were cycling on a busy road with no cycle lane. Construction is expected to be finished by autumn."
questions.opener: Find the most important points: WHAT has been decided, WHY, and when it will be finished (if there's room).
questions.answer: The municipality is building a new cycle path between the school and the town centre after complaints about dangerous cycling conditions. Construction is due to be finished by autumn.
steps: Identify the main event: the municipality has decided to build a cycle path.
Identify the cause: parents complained about dangerous cycling with no cycle lane.
Identify a detail that could be included if there's room: finished by autumn.
Filter out details that aren't necessary for the summary (e.g. exactly which road they used to cycle on) and combine the most important points into no more than two sentences.

questions.prompt: What strategies help you answer reading comprehension questions correctly?
questions.opener: A few habits that make a difference on tests.
questions.answer: Read the question before reading the text carefully, so you know what to look for. Separate the main message (the overall point of the text) from details (individual facts that support the point). For conclusions: base your answer only on what the text's details actually suggest — don't guess freely. Be suspicious of answer choices that are true in themselves but don't answer the question, or that claim more than the text supports.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"More and more schools are introducing phone bans during lessons. Students report that they find it easier to concentrate, and teachers see fewer conflicts over screen time. At the same time, critics argue that students miss the chance to learn to handle phones in a healthy way."

What is the main message of the text?
questions.opener: The text shows both benefits and an objection — which answer choice captures both sides?
choices: Phone bans are completely unproblematic
Phone bans seem to bring benefits for concentration, but there are also objections to banning phones entirely
Teachers would rather not have phone bans
Students do better without phones in every situation
questions.explanation: The text reports both positive effects (concentration, fewer conflicts) and the critics' objection (learning to handle phones) — a balanced summary must include both parts.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Simon knocked carefully on the door and waited. When no one answered he knocked again, a little harder this time. Finally he slipped the note he'd written under the door and walked away with his eyes lowered."

What can be concluded about Simon?
questions.opener: What does his lowered gaze say about how Simon feels as he walks away?
choices: Simon is angry and impatient
Simon seems disappointed that no one opened the door
Simon forgot why he came there
Simon enjoyed waiting
questions.explanation: Knocking twice, leaving a note, and walking away with lowered eyes suggests disappointment — the text never states this directly, but the details point that way.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The collection of recyclable glass has increased steadily over the past five years. Even so, large amounts of glass still end up in regular household waste, especially in areas without clear recycling information. Researchers believe better signage could increase recycling further."

What is the main message of the text?
questions.opener: The text mentions both an improvement and a remaining problem — which option captures the whole picture?
choices: Glass recycling already works perfectly
Despite progress, there is still room to improve glass recycling, for example through better information
No one cares about recycling glass
It is illegal not to recycle glass
questions.explanation: The text shows both that collection has increased and that problems remain, plus a concrete solution (signage) — that's the whole picture the text conveys.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"The swimming pool is closing temporarily for renovation of the pools. The work is expected to take six weeks, and the municipality is offering free bus rides to the neighbouring municipality's pool in the meantime."

Which headline best summarises the text?
questions.opener: A good headline captures WHAT is happening, HOW LONG, and what is offered in the meantime.
choices: The swimming pool is closing for good
The swimming pool is being renovated for six weeks, free bus rides offered in the meantime
The neighbouring municipality is building a new pool
The municipality is stopping swimming lessons
questions.explanation: The text is about a temporary closure for renovation (not permanent), with a time frame and a replacement offer — that's what headline 2 captures.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"Even though the recipe said forty minutes, Leo checked the oven every five minutes. He had already swapped the baking tray twice and re-measured the flour, just to be safe."

What can be concluded about Leo?
questions.opener: What do the repeated checks and swaps say about Leo's state of mind?
choices: Leo is very meticulous, perhaps even a little nervous about the baking
Leo doesn't care if the baking fails
Leo has baked the same recipe hundreds of times without any problems
Leo dislikes baking
questions.explanation: Checking the oven often, swapping the tray unnecessarily, and re-measuring ingredients "just to be safe" suggests meticulousness and a degree of nervousness — not indifference or routine.

questions.prompt: Summarise the text in no more than two sentences: "The youth centre has new opening hours after several visitors requested evening hours on Fridays. The new schedule means it's open until ten o'clock on Friday evenings, while the other days remain unchanged."
questions.opener: Find the most important points: WHAT has changed, WHY, and what has NOT changed (if there's room).
questions.answer: The youth centre is now open until ten o'clock on Fridays following requests from visitors. Opening hours on other days remain unchanged.
steps: Identify the main event: the youth centre has new opening hours on Fridays.
Identify the cause: visitors requested evening hours on Fridays.
Identify a detail that could be included if there's room: the other days are unchanged.
Filter out unnecessary details and combine the most important points into no more than two sentences.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer.

"A study shows that teenagers who use their phone just before falling asleep sleep 45 minutes less per night on average than those who put their phone away an hour before bedtime. The researchers stress that screen light isn't the whole explanation — the content itself, like social media, seems to keep the brain awake longer."

What is the main message of the text?
questions.opener: The text points to a connection AND nuances the cause — which answer includes both parts?
choices: Phone use close to bedtime is linked to shorter sleep, and it's about more than just screen light
Screen light is the only reason for worse sleep
Teenagers who use their phone sleep exactly as much as others
Social media should be banned entirely for young people
questions.explanation: The text shows the connection between phone use and shorter sleep, while also stressing that the explanation is more complex than just screen light — that captures the whole picture, unlike the other options which oversimplify or contradict the text.
